outline.description: Introduce the historical motivation behind recurrent networks, the vanishing gradient problem, and the core ideas of LSTM that solved it—constant error carousel and gating. Provide a step‑by‑step derivation of the classic scalar LSTM cell and discuss its mathematical properties, convergence guarantees, and practical implementations.
subtopics: Historical background: RNN limitations
Constant error carousel physics
Gate mechanisms (forget, input, output)
Scalar LSTM equations and forward pass
Weight and bias matrices
Activation functions (tanh, sigmoid)
Memory mixing via recurrent weight matrices
Examples of successful LSTM applications
outline.chapter_title: 2. Shortcomings of Classical LSTMs in Modern Contexts
outline.description: Examine the three major limitations that hinder LSTMs from matching Transformer success in large‑scale language modeling: inability to revise storage decisions, limited storage capacity due to scalar cells, and lack of parallelizability. Use illustrative synthetic tasks (nearest‑neighbor search, rare‑token prediction) to quantify these issues.
subtopics: Task 1: Nearest‑Neighbor Search – error analysis
Task 2: Rare Token Perplexity – capacity limits
The role of scalar cells in compression
Sequential dependency and memory mixing bottleneck
Why Transformers can bypass these limits
outline.chapter_title: 3. Exponential Gating – A Remedy for Storage Revision
outline.description: Present the concept of exponential activation for gates, accompanied by normalization and stabilization techniques. Show how this design permits dynamic revision of stored values during sequence processing.
subtopics: Motivation for exponential gates over sigmoid/softmax
Definition of input, forget, output gates with exp activation
Construction of normalizer state n_t
Stabilization using log–domain tricks (m_t)
Mathematical equivalence proof (no change to gradients)
Implementation pitfalls (overflow handling)
outline.chapter_title: 4. The sLSTM: Scalar Memory with Mixed Gates and Heads
outline.description: Detail the introduced sLSTM variant: a scalar memory cell that incorporates exponential gating and new memory mixing strategies including multi‑head designs. Discuss how memory mixing enables state tracking.
subtopics: Forward pass equations for sLSTM (c_t, h_t)
Role of multiple heads – intra‑head vs inter‑head mixing
Memory mixing via recurrent matrices ρ_z,i,f,o
Effect of permuting heads on expressivity
Comparison to vanilla LSTM in toy tasks
outline.chapter_title: 5. The mLSTM: Matrix Memory and Covariance Updates for Capacity Scaling
outline.description: Explain the extension to matrix‑valued memory cells that leverage covariance update rules for storing key–value pairs. Connect this design to Fast Weight Programmers, Bidirectional Associative Memories, and modern linear attention schemes.
subtopics: Matrix memory representation C_t ↔ d×d matrix
Covariance update rule C_t = C_{t-1} + v_k^T k_t
outline.chapter_title: 6. Integrating xLSTM Into Residual Backbone Architectures
